interactions.summary: Jiang keeps restating the consequentialist challenge that enormous good results should matter even if they come from fear, while a student insists that Piccarda's anxious self-protection shows the act still misses the point.

A student answers that quality beats quantity here because the same fearful soul will face the same decisive choice again until fear is actually overcome, and Jiang accepts that as part of the answer.
One student names Jiang's framing as consequentialist against virtue ethics, and another resolves the issue through a Constantine analogy in which God reads the spirit rather than tallying deeds.

claims.claim: Jiang presses a deliberately outcome-centered principle: if a person produces immense public good, motive alone seems insufficient to explain why God would still withhold redemption.
claims.temporal_scope: Jiang classroom pressure test stated on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: The class answer that begins to satisfy Jiang is that fear remains lodged in the soul, so no accumulation of good consequences repairs the deeper spiritual condition unless the fear itself is overcome.
A student explicitly frames the clash as consequentialism versus Aristotelian virtue ethics, where Dante's world cares more about the state of virtue than the external outcome.

The Constantine analogy argues that God does not finally judge by the inventory of deeds but by whether the spirit has actually reached salvation, so instrumental good works cannot substitute for inner transformation.
claims.temporal_scope: Student analogy endorsed by Jiang on 2026-06-15.

signature_moments.moment: The packet's cleanest answer says Piccarda can help a billion or a trillion people and still arrive back at the same decisive point until she overcomes fear itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: She can help a billion a trillion. She's still going to get back to that same spot
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the lecture's core insistence that spiritual failure is recursive until the inner cause changes.

signature_moments.moment: A student crystallizes the whole dilemma through Constantine: God does not see a ledger of deeds first but the state of the spirit behind them.
signature_moments.source_phrase: he does not see your deeds. He sees your salvation through your spirit
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the class a pop-cultural bridge that lands Jiang's difference between external benefit and inward redemption.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The student's shorthand for why masses of good deeds do not solve a soul-level failure of courage or faith.
A classroom analogy in which attempted self-salvation through good deeds fails because the deeds are not selfless and do not transform the spirit.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet sharpens the redemption debate into an ethics-and-salvation distinction: external outcomes matter less than whether fear has been transfigured inside the spirit.
